page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 architecture instance within the E2 server family. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The processor cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate a varied profile. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% of tested instances, while multi-core CPU performance falls in the average range. Memory bandwidth is consistently average, with read-only small block cached speeds at 645.66 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 35.27 GB/sec. However, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show poor performance, with gzip compression registering at 18.89 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 6.36 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10%. Geekbench multi-core and software compilation benchmarks align with average tier performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highcpu-16 offers a high vCPU-to-RAM density, making it a resource-efficient option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The lack of local storage and GPU hardware limits its utility for direct database hosting or deep learning training. It is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing tasks where multi-core CPU execution is required but memory demands remain low.
